Confluence over 8 weeks bear vs bull
Four rungs, and you only act on the top one. STAND DOWN, nothing is on. WATCH, one or two signals are true but they stand alone. SETUP, several are lining up. ACT, three of them have held for three sessions and they come from three different families, so it is not the same idea counted three times. A signal only counts once it has held three sessions, because one day in the zone is noise. Signals our lab rejected are left out of the count.
The three counts: firing = the condition is true at today's close, confirmed = it has been true 3 sessions in a row (this is what the bar counts), building = not true yet but close.
How to read each row: every signal is a checklist. Most of them need several things to be true at the same moment, so each line shows the condition, where it stands now and what it needs. A signal fires only when every box is ticked, which is why a number can sit well past its own trigger while the row still reads BUILDING. Some signals have two paths, either one arms them. ALERT (red bear / green bull) = it just fired, BUILDING = getting close, QUIET = nothing here yet. Widening? tells you whether the divergence is still growing or easing back. Click a row for the chart, the read, the Kerberos quote and how rare the signal is.

You want to see yen bid at the same time VIX is climbing and SPX is bleeding, because that three-way handshake is when real haven demand shows up. VIX up over the trailing month is in place, SPX down over the trailing month is in place, and the missing leg is FXY itself turning up over that same window.

The lab flags the solo FX read as marginal, so this one earns its keep only when yen joins the move. If FXY rolls over before VIX and SPX reverse, the setup dies on the vine.

Net dealer gamma on SPY sitting under zero is the fast-market regime, where dealers sell weakness and buy strength instead of dampening both. The gamma print is negative and has been for several sessions, with no missing condition to wait on.

This one is not formally backtested, so use it as the plumbing map: expect wider ranges, trend days, and sharper rug-pulls on any catalyst. It flips the moment gamma crosses back above zero and dealers go back to muting moves.

This is the high-yield credit stress read, the two-fifty-two-day z-score on BofA US High-Yield OAS, and it fires when spreads widen sharply from tight levels. The z-score is in place and nothing is missing, so credit is already flashing.

What kills it is spreads tightening back inside the band, which would pull the z-score below the trigger and remove the risk-off signal. This is an observation in our lab rather than a validated trade, but as a more direct credit tell than the HYG price row it earns a seat alongside the transports divergence in your bear stack.

Statuses recompute nightly from the EOD pipeline. Confirmed = 3 consecutive sessions in zone (the framework buffer rule: one day in zone is noise).
